entries.content: Anarchy is the ultimate goal and principled heart of communism: a classless, stateless society of free, cooperative association without coercion or hierarchy. Achieving anarchy requires a scientific analysis of class society, and the state as an instrument of class relations. The path to anarchy is realized through communism. When the state loses its social function and withers away, true anarchy finally emerges.
entries.name: Anarchy and Communism

entries.content: Communism is a classless, stateless, and moneyless society based on the principle 'from each according to their ability, to each according to their needs.' Achieving communism requires a transitional phase of socialism, during which the working class seizes the means of production, establishes a democratically planned economy, and systematically eradicates material scarcity and wage labor, causing state machinery and class divisions to wither away.
entries.name: Communism and Socialism

entries.content: Class struggle is the motor of human history under class society, arising from the structural contradiction between the capitalist class, who own the means of production, and the working class, who own only their labor power. Resolution of this contradiction requires the proletarian revolution, the expropriation of capital, and the socialization of production to establish a cooperative economy.
entries.name: Class Struggle

entries.content: Class consciousness is the objective recognition by workers of their distinct class interests, systemic exploitation, and collective historic power to abolish capitalism. It develops through living economic and political struggles, transitioning the working class from an unorganized collective into a self-conscious political force through strategic organization and theoretical understanding.
entries.name: Class Consciousness

entries.content: Under capitalism, formal legal freedoms remain constrained by economic coercion and wage labor. Genuine liberation requires collective liberation: the democratic control of productive forces by the associated producers, eliminating material insecurity to allow the full intellectual, creative, and physical development of every individual.
entries.name: Freedom and Liberation

entries.content: Bourgeois parliamentary democracy reflects the economic dominance of the capitalist class, limiting popular participation to periodic electoral cycles without democratic control over the economy. Workers' democracy is direct self-administration through workplace and community councils: delegates are subject to immediate recall, receive no more than the average skilled worker's wage, and combine legislative and executive functions to manage social production directly.
entries.name: Workers Democracy

entries.content: The dialectical relationship between means and ends is determined by what materially advances the emancipation of the working class. Strategy and tactics flow from the objective conditions of the class struggle. Overcoming the resistance of the capitalist class requires coordinated organization, social discipline, and collective power capable of dismantling entrenched coercive apparatuses.
entries.name: Means and Ends

entries.content: Historical materialism is the scientific method establishing that social consciousness, ideas, and institutions are determined by material conditions and the mode of production at a given stage of development. The economic foundation of society shapes its legal and political superstructure, and the development of productive forces drives historical transformation.
entries.name: Historical Materialism

entries.content: Dialectical materialism understands the universe and human society as dynamic, interconnected, and evolving through internal contradictions, the conflict of opposing forces, and quantitative accumulation leading to qualitative revolutionary leaps. The systemic contradictions within capitalist production drive recurrent economic crises and class confrontations.
entries.name: Dialectical Materialism

entries.content: Revolutionary theory provides a scientific analysis of political economy and class dynamics, serving as an essential foundation for action. Praxis is the synthesis of theory and action: theoretical analysis guides strategic intervention, while living struggles continuously test, refine, and ground theoretical understanding.
entries.name: Theory and Praxis

entries.content: The state is an apparatus of class rule and coercion emerging from irreconcilable class contradictions to protect the property relations of the ruling class. The working class replaces the capitalist state with a transitional workers' administration based on democratic councils to protect socialized production and expropriate capital. As class distinctions and material scarcity are eliminated, coercive state functions wither away into the democratic administration of resources.
entries.name: The State and Workers State

entries.content: Oppressions based on race, gender, nationality, and sexuality are structural features of class society, utilized to divide workers and extract super-profits through heightened exploitation. Eradicating oppression requires linking struggles against immediate discrimination with the unified class struggle to dismantle the economic system that generates and perpetuates social subjugation.
entries.name: Special Oppressions

entries.content: Imperialism is modern capitalism in its global monopoly stage, characterized by the export of capital, the domination of international financial cartels, and the geopolitical exploitation of the global working class. Meaningful decolonization and self-determination require dismantling imperialist economic relations and establishing international cooperative planning across liberated societies.
entries.name: Imperialism and Decolonization

entries.content: Democratic centralism combines complete internal democracy with unified collective action. All policies and leadership are democratically debated, decided, and elected by the membership. Once a collective decision is reached, all members act in disciplined coordination, concentrating organizational strength to match the centralized forces of class society.
entries.name: Democratic Centralism

entries.content: Social force is the collective power of the working class derived from its strategic role in producing societal wealth and maintaining modern infrastructure. Through conscious organization and common strategy, the working class transforms potential economic leverage into active political power capable of restructuring society.
entries.name: Social Force

entries.content: Direct action encompasses strikes, pickets, workplace occupations, and mass mobilizations through which workers exercise leverage at the point of production. Maximum effectiveness occurs when workplace struggles connect to a broader political strategy, uniting immediate economic conflicts with the systemic transformation of state power and property relations.
entries.name: Direct Action and Mass Action

entries.content: Praxis is the continuous dialectical unity of revolutionary theory and militant activity. Materialist theory provides strategic direction for intervention in the class struggle, while the empirical results of working-class action constantly test, refine, and validate revolutionary theory.
entries.name: Revolutionary Praxis

entries.content: Workers' control is the democratic direction of workplaces and production through councils, committees, and assemblies. Individual workplaces integrate into a comprehensive, democratically planned economy, coordinating resources, technology, and labor on a societal scale to meet human need.
entries.name: Workers Control and Planning

entries.content: The transitional program bridges the immediate struggles of the working class with the goal of socialist transformation. While supporting every immediate improvement in wages, safety, and living standards, the transitional method formulates demands that originate from current material conditions and lead to the collective democratic control of the economy.
entries.name: Reforms and Transitional Demands

entries.content: Dual power is a transitional phase in a revolutionary crisis characterized by the coexistence of two competing authorities: the existing capitalist state and emerging democratic workers' councils. Because two sovereign class authorities cannot permanently share power, the crisis resolves either through the workers' councils assuming full administration of society or through the restoration of ruling-class hegemony.
entries.name: Dual Power

entries.content: Workers' power is the objective capacity of the proletariat to enforce its class interests. Because the working class operates all production, transport, energy, and logistics, its collective refusal to work halts society, and its organized direction of these commanding heights of the economy is the foundation for a cooperative socialist society.
entries.name: Workers Power

entries.content: Socialist revolution is the mass transformation of society wherein the working class dismantles capitalist political and economic rule, brings major industries and finance into social ownership, and establishes democratic workers' management. This transition reorganizes society to satisfy human needs and initiates the historical progression toward stateless communism.
entries.name: Socialist Revolution

entries.content: Proletarian internationalism recognizes that modern capitalism is a global system of production and finance, making socialist transformation inherently international. Working-class interests transcend national borders, rejecting national chauvinism and imperialist war in favor of cross-border solidarity and coordinated global organizing.
entries.name: Revolutionary Internationalism

entries.content: The transition from capitalism to communism involves a temporary workers' state—the political rule of the working majority. During this phase, society brings major finance and industry under social ownership, organizes a planned economy, and resolves the contradictions of class society. As economic planning eliminates scarcity and class distinctions, the coercive apparatus of the state naturally withers away into the administration of public goods.
entries.name: The Transitional Period

entries.content: The revolutionary movement maintains active engagement within the mass labor movement and trade unions. Effective organizing grounds itself in the real day-to-day conditions of the working class, connecting immediate workplace grievances with the broader necessity of systemic political and economic transformation.
entries.name: Mass Labor Movement

entries.content: Cadre work involves the systematic activity of politically trained organizers within workplaces, educational institutions, and communities. Organizers participate directly in local struggles, providing strategic analysis, fostering solidarity, and developing working-class leadership.
entries.name: Cadre Work in the Class

entries.content: The vanguard organization represents the politically organized, class-conscious layer of the working class. It provides theoretical clarity and strategic continuity across fragmented struggles, helping unify workplace and social resistance into a coherent movement for political and economic power.
entries.name: Vanguard Organization

entries.content: Mass organizations—such as trade unions, tenant unions, and workers' councils (soviets)—unite broad layers of workers around immediate material interests. During revolutionary crises, workers' councils develop from defensive organs of economic struggle into self-governing bodies that administer production, distribution, and community defense.
entries.name: Mass Organizations and Soviets

entries.content: Theoretical clarity and unity provide the strategic foundation for effective political action. Grounding organization in scientific socialist analysis ensures consistent understanding of class dynamics, economic development, and historical lessons, enabling coherent strategy across diverse fronts of struggle.
entries.name: Theoretical Unity

entries.content: Strategic and tactical unity requires that once organizational strategy has been democratically debated and determined, all members act in unison. This disciplined collective alignment concentrates the social force of the organization and ensures maximal impact in the class struggle.
entries.name: Strategic and Tactical Unity

entries.content: Collective responsibility and revolutionary discipline are foundational principles of political organization. The organization is fully answerable to its membership, and each member is accountable to collective decisions, ensuring the mutual reliability required for effective action.
entries.name: Collective Responsibility

entries.content: Workers' democracy functions through recallable delegation. Delegates to workers' councils are elected directly from workplaces and communities, remain subject to immediate recall by their constituents, and receive wages comparable to the workers they represent, preventing the emergence of a detached bureaucratic caste.
entries.name: Recallable Delegation

entries.content: Cadre organization relies on a core of politically trained organizers surrounded by broad concentric circles of active participants, union militants, and community supporters. Internal functions balance democratic discussion and shared decision-making with disciplined collective implementation in public activity.
entries.name: Cadre Organization

entries.content: Continuous collective political education develops the theoretical knowledge and strategic skills needed for social transformation. Systematic study of political economy, history, and social dynamics equips organizers to understand structural contradictions and formulate effective strategies within the class struggle.
entries.name: Political Education

entries.content: The revolutionary program articulates the strategic analysis, objectives, and methods of the socialist movement. It connects immediate workplace and social struggles with long-term transformation, organizing workers around transitional demands that challenge private capital and build democratic self-management.
entries.name: The Revolutionary Program

entries.content: Trade unions serve as foundational defensive organizations of the working class. A rank-and-file strategy focuses on democratic member participation, direct workplace mobilization, and bottom-up control, ensuring unions act as democratic, militant instruments of class empowerment.
entries.name: Trade Union Strategy

entries.content: The United Front is a strategic method for building joint action between diverse working-class organizations, unions, and political tendencies for specific practical objectives, such as strikes or opposing authoritarian threats. It emphasizes unity in practical action while preserving the political independence and critical perspective of participating groups.
entries.name: The United Front

entries.content: Mass insurrection is the acute phase of a revolutionary situation where the organized working class mobilizes to transfer political and economic power to democratic workers' councils. It combines general strikes, mass workplace takeovers, and the neutralization of state coercive apparatuses to dismantle ruling-class authority.
entries.name: Mass Insurrection

entries.content: Post-revolutionary society organizes administration through councils (soviets) and communes emerging directly from popular struggle. These democratic councils coordinate regional and international economic planning, resource distribution, and public services based on bottom-up self-organization and delegate recallability.
entries.name: Soviets and Communes

entries.content: Mutual aid operates on two distinct levels: 1) As direct community solidarity and mutual defense during social and economic crises, meeting immediate human needs through collective cooperation; 2) As a broader strategy for structural societal transformation. While direct solidarity provides essential emergency support, systemic transformation requires collective political and economic leverage: organizing the working class to take control of the means of production, social infrastructure, and resource distribution, thereby resolving the material roots of scarcity permanently.
entries.name: Mutual Aid and Social Transformation
